newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain does not rule out expelling Cuban envoy.
newsitem.headline: Spain does not rule out expelling Cuban envoy.

text.p: Spain said on Wednesday it did not rule out expelling the Cuban ambassadress after Havana accused Madrid of meddling and withdrew its earlier approval for a new Spanish envoy.

"All options are open," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told a radio interviewer who asked him whether such an expulsion was possible. "Allow me not to speculate about measures which have not been decided and which, if and when they are decided, will first be communicated to the Cuban authorities."

Spain and Cuba came to diplomatic blows on Tuesday after months of rising tension. Havana accused Madrid of "flagrant interference" in its affairs and withdrew the approval it had already granted to a new Spanish ambassador.

Matutes described the move as "a big mistake" on Tuesday but later said Spain would not escalate the conflict. He repeated this pledge on Wednesday but accused Cuban leader Fidel Castro of creating a crisis to deflect attention from domestic trouble.
"It's typical of certain regimes, when they have internal difficulties, to invent a foreign enemy," Matutes said.

Since a conservative government took office in May after 13 years of Socialist rule, Spain has taken a tougher line against Castro and has begun nudging its European Union partners towards stronger demands for democracy in Cuba.
